lenses.verdict: This is a finished-looking product. The buyer flow (browse, shop, item sheet, cart dock, PayPal approve, receipt) and the seller flow (setup review, live, orders, AI brief, tracking) each have one clear primary action per screen, and status always pairs a dot with a word. Only one thing looks broken: the counter card's shop name collides with itself at desktop width. The rest is consistency. The assistant has two identities ("Shelfie assistant" on home, "Claude" on the shop page, "via Shelfie Assistant" in the seller's orders). The home chat offers a quick reply that contradicts the order on screen. The auth split screens show the logo twice. New shops use a photo of the paper price list as their avatar. The many blank areas in the full-page shots (the FAQ band and closing headline at 1440, How it works at 390, every shop section after Breads) are capture artifacts: on the live server at :3160 the hero chain's four cards and all menu sections render after scrolling, so I left them out.

findings.issue: The shop name on the counter card overlaps itself: "Marigold" sits on top of "Bakehouse" and the second line's bottom is clipped. The 390 render and the Share miniature look right.

At this width the line box resolves smaller than the glyphs. Check the computed line-height at 1440 (the card is about 480 px wide, so 10cqw is about 48 px). Either set an explicit leading in cqw (for example leading-[10.4cqw] beside text-[10cqw]) or drop the line clamp's fixed height and re-shoot.

strengths: The AI is visibly useful, not decorative. The order brief warns "Buyer mentions a nut allergy, but almond croissants contain nuts", checks PayPal's amount against the order, and turns the buyer's note into a pack list. The review step quotes what Claude read ("Cardamom bun 2 for $7") and asks the seller to confirm.

The buyer path is clean and honest. Item sheet, then a cart dock with an Assistant/Your order switch, then PayPal blue used only for "Approve $X on PayPal" with "Nothing is charged until you approve". Receipts open with a state icon, a display title and one primary action, then one grey summary well. The expired and awaiting states are equally clear.

The seller dashboard is well designed. Orders are grouped To prepare / Waiting for payment / Done with subtotals, status is always a dot and a word, there is one action per paid row, and the order detail's master list keeps context. The vermilion error, ochre warning and slate note colours stay distinct.

The public site is distinctive and on brand: a pomegranate wave hero with the staged Snap → Shop → Assistant → PayPal chain, real photography, and the home chat taking real orders with item cards from tool results.

Setup is built around the seller: a "Needs you" queue with Looks right / Fix / Remove, the original photo beside it for comparison, and the publish bar explaining why it is disabled ("Add your PayPal email to publish."), with inline errors that name the fix.
Phone layouts hold up everywhere reviewed: no horizontal scroll, a fixed four-tab bar in the seller app, a sticky order bar on shops, and full-width primaries.

findings.issue: The shop name on the full-size counter card overprints itself: "Marigold" and "Bakehouse" sit on top of each other with almost no line gap. At 390 and in the Share miniature it renders correctly.

findings.fix: In src/components/dashboard/CounterCard.tsx, line 49, the class order lets tailwind-merge drop `leading-[1.04]`, because `cardNameSize()` adds a later `text-[..cqw]` font-size and tailwind-merge treats font-size and line-height as conflicting. The miniature works only because it adds `leading-[1.04]` again at the end. Always put `leading-[1.04]` after `cardNameSize(name)` (drop the `miniature &&`), or have name-size.ts return `text-[Xcqw]/[1.04]`. Re-shoot counter-card-1440.
findings.evidence: counter-card-1440.png: the title glyphs collide at y≈385-435. CounterCard.tsx:49 is `cx('… leading-[1.04] …', cardNameSize(name), miniature && 'leading-[1.04]')`, and cardNameSize returns `text-[Ncqw]` (name-size.ts:9).

strengths: The palette discipline holds across about 100 screens. Pomegranate stays limited to the logo, active tabs, counts and the public bands, PayPal blue appears only on 'Approve $X on PayPal', errors use the separate vermilion, and status is always a dot plus a word.

The type scale is consistent. Figtree with display tracking gives a confident, product-grade hierarchy (the receipt's 'Paid. Marigold Bakehouse has your order.', the shop's display title, the auth headlines), and tabular figures line up in every total.

Interaction states are thorough: visible 2 px focus rings (white on the pomegranate FAQ, ink elsewhere), skeletons shaped like the orders list, inline errors that name the fix, disabled Publish with the reason as a link, cart-error and PayPal-unreachable banners, and a reduced-motion path checked by tests.

Responsive work is real rather than squeezed. The shop goes from 2 to 4 tile columns by container query, the cart and assistant share one dock with a switch from 1024 px, there are true bottom sheets on phones, the order rows reflow, and the dashboard swaps sidebar for tab bar.

The seller dashboard reads as a real product. Orders are grouped with subtotals, the AI brief surfaces the nut-allergy conflict where the seller sees it, the order detail separates PayPal IDs from the human summary, and the counter card and Share page tie the agent door to the physical shop.
The photography and illustration system makes empty or partial menus still look deliberate: real photos, example photos honestly labelled, and category drawings as the fallback.
lenses.verdict: The craft is strong and coherent, close to submission quality. One thing looks plainly broken: the overlapping shop name on the full-size counter card, a one-line tailwind-merge ordering fix. One visible AI misstep: the home chat always suggests "Make it pickup instead", even after Claude says the order is pickup. After those, the biggest wins are coherence fixes a judge would notice while clicking around. The assistant is named "Shelfie assistant" on the home page and "Claude" on the shop. The auth screens show the logo twice. The dock reads "Your order 0" right after an order is placed. Repairs/Services labels differ between Browse and the shop. The help and legal content doesn't line up with its header. The per-section Reveal on the shop menu leaves full-page captures half blank. Everything left is small polish, and each Should-fix is S effort, so a focused hour clears all of them.

findings.issue: The shop name on the counter card is drawn with its two lines overlapping: "Marigold" and "Bakehouse" are stacked about 15 px apart at a font size of about 48 px. The cause is in CounterCard.tsx line 49: `cx('… leading-[1.04] …', cardNameSize(name), miniature && 'leading-[1.04]')`. tailwind-merge treats `text-[10cqw]` as a font-size class, and a font-size class later in the list removes the earlier `leading-*`. I checked this with the repo's own `cn`: the output is `line-clamp-3 font-display font-extrabold text-[10cqw]`, with no leading. Only the miniature adds the leading back, so the full card falls back to the body's fixed line-height. At 390 the font is about 30 px, so the overlap is hard to see there.

lenses.verdict:
Two Must-fix bugs. The counter-card title overlaps itself at 1440 because tailwind-merge drops `leading-[1.04]` (CounterCard.tsx:49); I confirmed this by running the repo's own `cn`. The home chat's real Claude turn offers "Make it pickup instead" on an order that is already pickup (hard-coded in landing/chat/order.ts:73). Both are under 20 minutes to fix.

Part C 2026 banned-pattern counts per screen:
- **0:** home, shop, item sheet, cart and dock, consoles, receipts, orders, order detail, share, help, 404.
- **1 (pass):** browse (wall of identical cards, softened by real photos), dashboard-settings and account (grey helper lines).
- **2 (fail):** setup-review and review-paypal-email, for a grey explanatory sentence under almost every element plus a box around everything. Both also put pills on every thumbnail.

"Images, not stand-ins" passes everywhere. The Real-product check passes on every screen except counter-card at 1440, where the overlapping title makes it fail until it is fixed.

The main remaining generated tells:
- The buyer assistant has two different identities ("Shelfie assistant" with a bot avatar on home, "Claude" with the awning on shops).
- The shop avatar is a crop of the cover photo it sits on.
- The phone home page repeats its 3 numbered steps.

The full-page shots for home and shop-seeded look empty only because scroll-reveal content was never in view during capture. The viewport shots render correctly, so don't use those full-page images in submission material.

merged.issue: At 1440 the hero chain's caption pills wrap unevenly: '1. Snap / your menu' and '3. AI / shoppers order' take two lines while '2. Get a live shop' takes one, so the pills differ in height and width. On phones the hero's numbered rows (1 Snap your menu, 2 Get a live shop, 3 AI shoppers order) are followed straight away by How it works's own numbered steps (1. Snap your price list, 2. AI shoppers order, 3. Get paid on PayPal), and the two lists disagree on names and numbers. At 390 about 120 px under the rows is an unreadable brown blur of the photo.

merged.fix: In landing/HeroChain.tsx, give the captions whitespace-nowrap with a slightly smaller size at lg, or a fixed two-line min-height so all pills match. Drop the numerals from the hero captions, or make the phone rows one 'menu → shop → order' strip. Align the step names with How it works. Trim the hero's bottom padding at 390 so the wave follows the chain.

verdicts.note: counter-card-1440.png shows 'Marigold' and 'Bakehouse' overlapping inside the card's title. In CounterCard.tsx:49, cx (which is cn, so clsx plus tailwind-merge) gets 'leading-[1.04]' before cardNameSize()'s 'text-[10cqw]'. tailwind-merge then drops the leading, and only the miniature adds it back.
verdicts.fix: In src/components/dashboard/CounterCard.tsx:49 put the leading after the size class for every card, not only the miniature: cx('line-clamp-3 font-display font-extrabold tracking-display [overflow-wrap:anywhere]', cardNameSize(name), 'leading-[1.04]'). Then update the doc comment at lines 20-22. Re-shoot counter-card-1440 and check the print preview.

verdicts.note: Partly confirmed. The shop console greets 'Hi! I'm Claude' with the header 'Claude, for Marigold Bakehouse', while the home chat says 'Shelfie assistant'. The visual differences (BotMark, blush chips, pomegranate Send) are the owner-approved home-chat look (DESIGN.md 'Home chat', DECISIONS run 10), so they are not a defect. The dashboard part is wrong: both in-app consoles record CONSOLE_AGENT_NAME 'shelfie-assistant' (shown as 'Shelfie Assistant'). The 'via Claude' rows are external Claude MCP clients, so those labels are accurate. The real mismatch is that the shop console calls itself Claude but its orders show 'via Shelfie Assistant'.
verdicts.fix: Rename only the shop console's voice. In src/components/shop/BuyerConsole.tsx:471/473, and in its header subtitle 'Claude, for {shop}', use 'the Shelfie assistant' (optionally 'powered by Claude'), matching HomeChat.tsx:167 and the recorded agent name. Keep the home chat's approved look, and don't change how agent names are recorded.

verdicts.note: What the finding describes is visible: browse-1440.png avatars are crops of their own covers, and setup-live-1440.png shows the price-list scan as the avatar in the sidebar and on the Live card. But the order logo > cover crop > menu photo > drawing, and the avatar overlapping the cover's lower edge, are a written human decision (DECISIONS 6 Nov 'images, never text stand-ins') and are spelled out in DESIGN.md 'The shop's picture'. So this is a deliberate rule, not a bug.
verdicts.fix: Raise it with the owner rather than change it unilaterally. If they agree, in src/lib/domain/avatar.ts shopAvatar(), rank the first item's picture (pictureOf) or the category drawing above menuPhotoSrc. Then update DESIGN.md 'The shop's picture' to match.
